4. Material -The polygon shall be made of high tirade steel,~hardened and subjected to a suitable heat treatment for dimensional stabilization. A minimum hardness value of 700 HV is recommended [see IS : 1501-I 968 Methods for Vickers hardness test for steel ( firsf revision )]. The polygon can also be of composite structure with hardened steel strips being inserted on to the steel body. 5. 9.3 Each polygon shall be supplied with certificates in which the error of the angles between adjacent faces and the cumulative angles from the datum face (see Appendix 4) shall be given to an accuracy / of 61 second of arc or finer. 10. c) maker's name or trade-mark, d) the top surface and the supporting e) (i) surface,

APPENDIX ( Clause 9.1 )

A

IDENTIFICATION OF POLYGON

FACES

The faces of the polygons have to be identified to enable the resultd of its calibration to be recorded and subsequently applied in the use of the polygon, Each face is identified by engraving on the top surface the nominal angles between the face and a datum face. (The datum face can be any one of the working faces. ) The angles are the nominal external angles of the polygons or the nominal angles between the normals to the faces. However, with polygon having large number of faces and in all cases where these nominal angles are not a whole number of degrees, the faces are identified by a series of numbers from 1 upwards.

IS : 6987 - 1973 EXPLANATORY NOTE

The precision polygons are made of -hardened steel. The angle ~between the peripheral faces constitute in a material form the division of 360" into any number of very accurate equal parts according to the number of faces on the polygons. In the preparation Moy/SCMI/l ratory ( Teddington of this standard, assistance has been derived from: for an NPL steel precision polygon, National Physical Labo-
